title: MTV waste audit receipt, version 1
description:
A machine-readable statement of where an agent session's tokens went and how much of that was waste. The markdown receipt is the human view of this same object.

Every field here is a number, an identifier, or a bounded enum. There is deliberately no free text: a receipt is meant to be shareable, and prompts, code and paths stay on the machine that produced it.

schema_version.description: Bumped only for a breaking change. New optional fields do not bump it.

id.description: Session identifier as recorded by the agent runtime.

source_filename.description: Filename only, never a path. The directory above a session log routinely names an employer, a client, or an unreleased product.

audited_on.description: Date the audit ran, not the date the session happened.

data_provenance.description: 'redacted-real' is derived, not asserted: redaction is unconditional, so the value states what the tool did. Anything produced from a synthetic fixture is 'fixture'.

totals.description: What the run cost in total, before any waste attribution.

usd.description: Blended across cache rates. Depends on the price table — see price_table_version.

channels.description: Waste attributed per spend channel. Every channel key is always present, with zeros when the rule found nothing — an absent key would be indistinguishable from a rule that did not run.

recoverable.description: What could plausibly have been avoided. An upper bound until a counterfactual replay confirms it.

verified.description: False means this is an estimate, not a measured saving. The 'model' channel is excluded from the total until a replay on a cheaper model confirms it.

replay_status.description: NOT_RUN is the honest default: the counterfactual replay runner is an interface with a stub implementation.

projection.description: Monthly extrapolation. Assumption-driven, so it is optional and carries its assumption.

top_items.description: The largest individual sources of waste. Identified by block id and turn range so they can be located in the local log — never by their content.

emitter.description: Who produced this receipt. Set by tools other than mtv-audit that implement this schema.

channelName.description:
retry: a failure trace re-sent after the tool already failed.
clean: stale context re-read — blocks no longer relevant to the goal.
comm: full-state rebroadcast where a diff would have done.
deep: thinking spent on a step that did not need it.
stop: tokens spent after the job was already done.
model: a trivial step sent to the top-tier model. Flagged, never counted as recoverable without a replay.

dial.description: How aggressively a rule calls something waste. Totals must be monotonic across them: saver >= balanced >= optimizer. A stricter dial never claims less waste than a looser one.
